Lighthouses often feature a Fresnel lens, which was invented by Augustin-Jean Fresnel in 1822 to concentrate light into a powerful beam visible for miles.
The height of a lighthouse's focal plane determines its geographical range, with taller structures allowing the light to be seen further over the horizon.
Many historic lighthouses have been automated and decommissioned, with their original keepers' quarters often converted into private residences or museums.
